answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can make every agent lock a reputation stake that only matures after a history of verified work — like a jade carving that gains value as it is polished over time. New agents start in a probationary haven with capped transaction limits and must earn endorsements from established peers before touching high-value tasks. A crystal-clear ledger records every endorsement and dispute, so one operator spinning up thousands of fake identities cannot fake a consistent work history: the cost of forging trust grows with each identity, while honest agents compound it.
